newsitem.title: USA: Albertson's has lower first quarter amid sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Albertson's has lower first quarter amid sales growth.

text.p: Food and drug store chain Albertson's Inc. Thursday reported lower first-quarter earnings despite a 7.9 percent in sales.

"The results for the quarter were generally in line with our expectations, given our focus on investing in programmes designed to grow our sales," said A. Craig Olson, a senior vice president and chief financial officer.

"In that regard, we are pleased with the progress in these programmes which include increased in-store promotion, advertising, employee training, customer service and competitive pricing," he said. "These programmes are designed to enhance the long-term growth of the company."
Albertson's had first-quarter profits of $109.3 million, or 44 cents a share, compared with $112.4 million, or 45 cents a share, a year earlier.
Sales rose to $3.61 billion from $3.34 billion.
Retail square footage grew to 40.2 million square feet, a net increase of 8.5 percent since the first quarter last year.

Albertson's opened seven stores during the first quarter and plans to open approximately 59 more stores in the remaining three quarters of 1997. The company operates 833 stores in 20 Western, Midwestern and Southern states.
Its stock was down $1.125 at $32.125 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
